correctness.rationale: The invariant Walsh projection formula gives λ=E|K_N| with K_N=(S_N²−N)/2, where S_N is the sum of N independent signs. By mean zero, its L1 norm is twice the negative central mass. The identity K_N(k)C(N,k)=C(N,2)[C(N−2,k)−2C(N−2,k−1)+C(N−2,k−2)] telescopes over the exact parity-aware negative band to the stated one-boundary binomial difference, then the equivalent rational prefactor follows algebraically. Uniform Stirling in the window r=√N−δ, 0≤δ<2, combined with the prefactor gives cN+c(1/6−(δ−1)²)+O(N^(−1/2)). Subsequence squares δ=0 and squares+1 δ→1 attain the extrema. Fresh independently coded direct exact rational Walsh averages matched the exact boundary formula for N=2..100; N=10000,10001,40000,40001,90000,90001 matched the predicted order-one phase to the stated error scale. This does not use finite checks as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The projection constant is a natural Banach-space invariant; its exact finite degree-two formula and uniform lattice-phase correction sharpen the previously determined leading linear growth, reveal nonconvergence of the order-one remainder and give sharp limsup/liminf. A precise finite-size oscillation is mathematically motivated, useful for comparisons and not mere arbitrary small-case computation.
value.risk: Result is limited to homogeneous Walsh chaos degree two and does not imply analogous formulas for higher degrees.

final_claim: For N≥2 the absolute projection constant of homogeneous second Walsh chaos equals the explicit boundary binomial expression with parity-adjusted \(r_N\), and satisfies \(\lambda_N=cN+c(1/6-(\delta_N-1)^2)+O(N^{-1/2})\) uniformly, where \(c=\sqrt{2/(\pi e)}\), \(\delta_N=\sqrt N-r_N\in[0,2)\). The order-one remainder has limsup \(c/6\) and liminf \(-5c/6\).
limitations: Real Banach-space absolute projection constant of the second homogeneous Walsh level only.
